Gaganyaan in final phase, says Isro chief

NEW DELHI: The first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-N1) is ready for a maiden launch in the "first quarter of next year", Isro chairman V Narayanan said on Tuesday. He also said govt is fast-tracking satellite launches in collaboration with startups "in a big way" as Isro currently has only 56 space assets in orbit.Talking about foreign collaboration, the Isro chairman said, "India is collaborating with 64 countries... At least 434 satellites for 34 countries have lifted off from Indian soil during the last 12 years."Speaking on the sidelines of the 5th India International Space Conference in Delhi, Isro chief V Narayanan said, “Earlier, it was only Isro that built PSLV with the support of industry. Now, an L&T and HAL consortium has been given five PSLVs (to build). So, the first rocket PSLV-N1 is getting ready and we are targeting to launch it by the first quarter of next year.” Isro’s arm NSIL signed a contract with the consortium in Sept 2022 for Rs 860 crore for five PSLV rockets.Narayanan said, “We need to build a lot of space assets for communication, navigation and earth observation. This can’t be done by govt sector (alone). Isro and INSPACe are hand-holding private companies and you will see its benefit five years from now.Today, from one startup, their number has come to 440+.”Pointing out that “Gaganyaan is not late”, he said, “It is a technology-intensive activity. We are in the final phase. The rocket and other items are ready. We’re working on the orbital module. At the earliest opportunity, it will be launched.” He said, “Isro and Semiconductor Lab in Chandigarh have developed a Vikram processor. Vikram-32 chip has come out, and we are going to induct it.”
Article Summary: Gaganyaan in final phase, says Isro chief V Narayanan. He also said govt is fast-tracking satellite launches in collaboration with startups "in a big way" Isro currently has only 56 space assets in orbit.

NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry is proposing a series of measures to address the problem of uninsured vehicles on roads, including introducing a single premium for four- and six-year insurance policies for cars and two-wheelers, respectively.Separately, the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has asked road transport and petroleum ministries to launch a pilot of the ‘no insurance, no fuel’ initiative at five petrol pumps each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh which have automated number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that can identify vehicles and help verify their insurance status.TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry is also working on the plan to link premiums to traffic offences recorded against vehicle owners in the previous year.The proposed changes are aimed at encouraging more vehicle owners to maintain valid insurance coverage and improving compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act. Under the proposal, insurance premiums could increase based on specific traffic violations recorded against a vehicle in the preceding year, making repeated offenders pay more for insurance.The ministry is also examining options to revise the base insurance rates for specified vehicle categories, including electric vehicles, as part of a broader review of the existing premium structure.Insurance data show that nearly 25 crore active vehicles have valid insurance, which is around 81% of the vehicles that are currently running across the country. While over 90% of heavy commercial vehicles have valid insurance, it’s around 88% in the case of cars. The compliance is least at around 57% in case of three-wheelers and it’s around 80% in case of two-wheelers.Supreme Court had earlier issued directions to govt to examine measures to ensure that vehicles plying on roads have valid insurance coverage. Third-party motor insurance is mandatory under the Motor Vehicles Act. Vehicles without valid insurance pose a serious risk in case of crashes, leaving accident victims and their families vulnerable to inadequate compensation.
Article Summary: Road transport ministry is proposing a series of measures to address the problem of uninsured vehicles on roads. The proposed changes are aimed at encouraging more vehicle owners to maintain valid insurance coverage. The Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has asked road transport and petroleum ministries to launch a pilot of the ‘no insurance, no fuel’ initiative.

NEW DELHI: The Centre has allotted a Type-7 government bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama and his office, Gaden Phodrang, providing a permanent base for his visits to the national capital. Members of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile Tuesday described the move as a significant gesture of support towards the spiritual leader and the Tibetan community.Though housing and urban affairs ministry officials did not respond to queries, it is learnt that the ministry had transferred the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane to the ministry of external affairs last year after receiving a request. People aware of the development said usually, such transfers of accommodation are initially for three years and can be extended.According to news agency ANI, speaker of the Tibetan parliament-in-exile Dolma Tsering described the development as "very welcome news". She said the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital more convenient and provide greater comfort during his stay in Delhi.Welcoming the decision, Tibetan parliament-in-exile member and standing committee member Choedak Gyatso said, "government of India has given us refuge when we had no country.We lost our country, and it gave us Dharamshala when we had no land and gave us schools and many institutions that can preserve our culture."Recalling his recent official visit to Delhi, during which he met MPs, Gyatso said he had personally visited the bungalow along with the Tibetan deputy speaker and described the opportunity as a great honour.Gaden Phodrang, the Dalai Lama's office, was registered as a private trust in India in 2011 after he voluntarily relinquished political authority in favour of an elected Tibetan leadership. The trust is responsible for preserving the institution of the Dalai Lama and supporting his spiritual and humanitarian work.

NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation under the framework of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).According to news agency ANI, the Iranian delegation was led by Alireza Tootonchian, director general for multilateral and International economic cooperation. He met Thelma John David, MEA joint secretary (Indo-Pacific), in the national capital. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping.In a post on X, the Iranian embassy in India said that Tootonchian and deputy director general Abolfazl Azizi Panah held discussions with David on multilateral cooperation under the IORA framework.The meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday. Foreign ministers from member countries are expected to attend the gathering to discuss regional cooperation and strategic priorities in the Indian Ocean Region.India is also hosting the 29th IORA Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) meeting ahead of the ministerial gathering. The two-day meeting began on Wednesday.The council of ministers is IORA's highest decision-making body and comprises foreign ministers of member states. It provides strategic and policy direction to the association, reviews progress in regional cooperation and identifies new areas of collaboration.The committee of senior officials is the organisation's second-highest decision-making body. It comprises senior government representatives who oversee the implementation of ministerial decisions, review recommendations and coordinate IORA's work programmes.Meanwhile, the European union (EU) and IORA held their first high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi on Tuesday. Representatives from several Indian Ocean countries participated in discussions on improving maritime surveillance, tackling piracy and trafficking, and protecting important shipping routes.The European union organised the event with support from its project 'Enhancing the EU's security cooperation in and with Asia and the Indo-Pacific' (ESIWA+) and in coordination with its Delegation to India.Addressing the gathering, EU ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet reaffirmed the bloc's commitment to expanding security and defence cooperation with regional partners. He also stressed the importance of sharing information to tackle maritime threats.Paquet said maritime security was a shared priority for the EU and IORA, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime crime and other challenges at sea.He also highlighted the Indian ocean's importance to global trade, warning that maritime insecurity could disrupt international supply chains and affect economic growth across the region.Representatives from IORA member states and dialogue partners, including India, Australia, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and Saudi Arabia, attended the roundtable.Participants discussed improving maritime domain awareness, strengthening policy dialogue and expanding cooperation through EU-supported initiatives such as EUCRIMARIO, EnMAR+ and ESIWA+.The discussions also covered the European Union naval force's operation ATALANTA, which works to improve maritime security in the western Indian ocean and red sea. The operation focuses on deterring piracy, protecting vulnerable vessels and monitoring illegal maritime activities.India assumed the IORA chairmanship from Sri Lanka in November 2025 for the 2025-2027 term. Its chairmanship theme is "innovation, openness, resilience and adaptability in the Indian ocean region".
Article Summary: Iranian delegation meets officials from India's Ministry of External Affairs. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping. Meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water, with the results expected to take at least one to two months, FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani said.The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts to examine various food categories and ensure compliance with prescribed standards."That process has started, and we're doing it across the country. The results will take at least a month or two," Punhani told reporters.He clarified that packaged drinking water was not selected for any specific reason but was part of the regulator's broader surveillance programme."Last year, we took up dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, sugary drinks and other products. So, water is also part of the process," he added.Separately, Punhani stressed the need for food businesses to follow ethical advertising practices, particularly when making claims about their products and promoting them.He emphasised that the regulator was not looking at the issue solely from a legal perspective and urged industry players to consider the ethical dimensions of advertising."The idea is not that it's only the legal part of it. It is also the ethical part of it," he said, calling on the industry to focus on responsible advertising practices.Punhani's remarks and the nationwide surveillance exercise come amid regulatory action against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International over a sample collected from its Goa facility.On November 23, the FSSAI granted sanction to prosecute the company after a regulatory sample was initially found non-compliant with the prescribed limits for bromate and declared unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.Following an appeal by the company, the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further examination, which also declared it unsafe after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).However, the FSSAI clarified on Monday that the action was limited to a single sample from one batch, numbered GO 270, collected from the company's plant at Verna Electronic City in South Goa.The authority also issued an order prohibiting the sale of the concerned batch under Section 36(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.Bisleri International subsequently welcomed the clarification, maintaining that the sales prohibition applied only to the specific batch manufactured at its Goa plant on September 27, 2025.The company stated that it produces more than 50,000 batches annually and that no stocks of the particular batch were currently available in the market. It also maintained that retesting found bromate levels below the permissible limit.
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has launched a nationwide surveillance exercise to assess the quality of packaged drinking water. The exercise is being carried out across the country as part of the food safety regulator's ongoing efforts. The drive comes amid the ongoing Bisleri row.

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP), accusing its leadership of practising family-centric politics and failing to respect the sentiments of devotees of Lord Ram.“Radhe Radhe is just the beginning. Time for Ram Naam Satya is approaching for the SP,” Adityanath said, taking a swipe at the party during an interview at the ABP Conclave, as cited by news agency PTI.The chief minister also targeted SP president Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed visit to Ayodhya, saying those who tried to sail in two boats would eventually drown.CM Adityanath said the SP leadership should apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus for the firing on devotees in the 1990s. “If the SP leadership had shown some wisdom in the 1990s, bullets would not have been fired at Ram devotees. They should now apologise to Ram devotees and Hindus,” he said, according to a press statement of the interview.Explaining his remark, CM Yogi said greetings should reflect local religious traditions, with 'Radhe Radhe' appropriate in Mathura, 'Jai Shri Ram' in Ayodhya and 'Har Har Mahadev' in Kashi.He added that 'Ram Naam Satya' was traditionally associated with a person's final journey.Taking aim at the SP's PDA slogan, CM Adityanath described it as “Parivar Development Authority”, alleging that the party's politics was limited to the interests of its own family.He also criticised the SP-Congress alliance, claiming it had run into trouble even before the elections because of differences over seat-sharing. The chief minister pointed to the two parties announcing candidates while negotiations were still under way.The seat-sharing discussions have remained inconclusive after two rounds of meetings. The SP announced five candidates on Tuesday, prompting criticism from Congress leaders.Congress's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the SP should have waited until the negotiations were over. “They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over),” he told PTI, while expressing hope that the discussions would proceed in the right direction.Congress MP Imran Masood also questioned the SP's move, saying simultaneous talks and candidate announcements suggested that the party was not serious about the negotiations. He said the Congress would consult its leadership on whether discussions should continue.SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, meanwhile, urged the Congress to focus on “winning equations” rather than the number of seats. He asked the party to share a list of constituencies it was interested in contesting beyond the 26 seats proposed by the SP, so that both parties could jointly assess which candidate was best placed to win.Adityanath said the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance allies would contest the elections together, with candidates selected through the party's established process.On the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, CM Adityanath said the exercise was necessary to remove the names of deceased voters and people who had shifted elsewhere.“Every eligible Indian citizen should have a place on the voter list, but a foreign national cannot have voting rights,” he said, accusing the SP of supporting infiltrators while questioning Indian citizens.The chief minister also highlighted what he described as Uttar Pradesh's economic transformation since 2017, saying the state's economy, per capita income and budget had grown more than threefold. He claimed the state had moved from being a “BIMARU” state to a growth engine.Contrasting the state's industrial landscape with that under previous governments, CM Adityanath said Uttar Pradesh had moved from illegal country-made pistol and bomb factories to manufacturing revolvers, rifles and BrahMos missiles.He said the state had received investment proposals worth Rs 50 lakh crore and introduced 36 sector-specific policies to attract investors. Uttar Pradesh, he added, accounted for 55 per cent of India's mobile phone production and 60 per cent of electronic component manufacturing.The chief minister said the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) sector and the One District One Product (ODOP) initiative were providing employment to 3.25 crore people. He also claimed that housing disputes involving four lakh homebuyers had been resolved through dialogue between builders and buyers.On employment, he said the government had issued nearly 9.75 lakh appointment letters to young people and aimed to increase the number to 10.5 lakh by January 26.Warning those threatening the safety of women, traders and investors, he said people who cast an evil eye on daughters, traders and women moving on the streets would have only two destinations — “jail or jahannum”.CM Yogi described Prime Minister Narendra Modi as his role model and said he was an ordinary party worker who would discharge whatever responsibility was assigned to him.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath accuses Samajwadi Party leadership of practising family-centric politics. He also criticises the SP-Congress alliance, claiming it had run into trouble even before the elections because of differences over seat-sharing. He claims Uttar Pradesh has moved from being a 'BIU' state to a growth engine.

Article Title: ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic
Article Text:
(Representative image): The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories, drawing data from over 81,000 households and analysing over 1.7 lakh blood samples.

NEW DELHI: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic, while nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in vitamin B12, pointing to a wider nutritional challenge that goes beyond iron deficiency, a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has found.The findings fill a key data gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which did not include anaemia estimates. Government had subsequently said these would be drawn from an independent ICMR survey based on venous blood samples.The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition's SAMPADA survey for 2023-25 found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years. NFHS-5 reported a prevalence of 57 per cent among women in the same age group. The figures, however, are not directly comparable because the surveys covered different groups of women and used different testing methods.State-wise estimates showed sharp regional disparities, with Andaman and Nicobar recording the highest prevalence at 81.2 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years.The burden was also high in other groups. Anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19 years.Among children, 41.8 per cent of those aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent of those aged 5-9 years were anaemic. The prevalence was 43.6 per cent among pregnant women and 58.1 per cent among lactating women. Among adult men aged 20-59 years, it stood at 22 per cent.B12 deficiency was more widespread among adolescents, affecting 65.4 per cent of girls and 66.1 per cent of boys. It was found in 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of adult men aged 20-59 years. The prevalence stood at 63.1 per cent among pregnant women and 51.8 per cent among lactating women.Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, despite anaemia affecting 46.3 per cent and 55.9 per cent of these groups, respectively. Iron deficiency itself remained common, affecting 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age, 29.6 per cent of pregnant women and 23 per cent of children aged 12-59 months, compared with 10 per cent for adolescent boys."Not all anaemia is caused by nutritional deficiencies such as iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, chronic kidney disease, tuberculosis and cancer can also cause anaemia. Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," said Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology, AIIMS."We have been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme to develop simple algorithms to identify such cases," Seth added.The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories, drawing data from over 81,000 households and analysing over 1.7 lakh blood samples.
Article Summary: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic. Nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in vitamin B12. The findings fill a key data gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which did not include anaemia estimates.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
