Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Coca-Cola bought Gold Spot from Parle Bisleri in 1993, but discontinued it in 2000 to make way for Fanta; 26 years later it is set to be re-launched with a low- or no-sugar version amid rising competi
Article Text:
Unlike colas, which account for the bulk of the Rs 60,000 crore aerated drinks market, orange-flavoured beverages represent a relatively small share of overall sales. (Image for representative purpose only)

The return of Gold Spot

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Coca-Cola is preparing to bring back its orange carbonated drink Gold Spot after a gap of 26 years. The move comes at a time when the competition in the beverage market intensifies and demand for sugar-free products gathers pace, people familiar with the development said.Coca-Cola’s Indian arm bought Gold Spot in 1993 from Ramesh Chauhan, the owner of Parle Bisleri, along with Thums Up and Limca. The Atlanta-headquartered beverage company discontinued Gold Spot shortly after the acquisition to make room for Fanta, its global brand.“Gold Spot is returning as a low-sugar, no-sugar drink, so it won’t cannibalise on Fanta. It is expected to be on shelves starting next week,” one of the executives aware of the developments, told ET.Meanwhile, photographs and posts circulating on social media over the weekend showed former India cricket captain MS Dhoni and his wife with cans of Gold Spot. The posts went viral, although it remains unclear whether Dhoni has been signed on as the brand’s endorser.Gold Spot, which was promoted with the tagline ‘zing thing’, was withdrawn by Coca-Cola in 2000 as the company sought to make way for Fanta.“Market share gain of legacy brands being revived after a long gap depends entirely on adequate investments in distribution, product and go-to-market,” the executive cited above told the financial daily.“Some like Thums Up, however, have always led the Indian cola market, ahead of Coca-Cola’s own global brand Coke as well as rival Pepsi, even without investments in the early years.”Unlike colas, which account for the bulk of the Rs 60,000 crore aerated drinks market, orange-flavoured beverages represent a relatively small share of overall sales.Gold Spot’s planned comeback comes at a time when consumers are increasingly turning towards healthier alternatives. The market is also facing intense competition, while New Delhi has proposed a regulatory requirement for red hexagonal labels on the front of all food and beverage packs to indicate excessive levels of sugar, salt and fat.In recent months, brands such as Reliance Consumer Products’ Campa, Lahori Zeera and Bindu Zeera, along with newer products including ITC’s Coconut Cola and Veera Foods’ Zyro, have challenged the long-standing dominance of Coca-Cola and PepsiCo in India for the first time.At the same time, sales of Coca-Cola’s mid-calorie and sugar-free beverages have risen sharply. These include zero- and no-sugar variants under its flagship Coke, Sprite and Thums Up brands, as well as Schweppes, Powerade and Rimzim. Sales of these products have doubled this year compared with last year, according to two bottling industry associates.The associates said diet and light beverages now account for more than 60% of Coca-Cola’s annual sales, up from around 30% last year.Varun Beverages, PepsiCo’s bottling associate, has also recorded a sharp increase in demand for beverages with reduced or no sugar. Sales of these products doubled to 88% of its total volumes in the July-September 2026 quarter, compared with 44% in the corresponding period a year earlier. The category also includes water and sodas.
Article Summary: Coca-Cola’s Indian arm bought Gold Spot in 1993 from Ramesh Chauhan, the owner of Parle Bisleri, along with Thums Up and Limca. Atlanta-headquartered beverage company discontinued Gold Spot shortly after the acquisition to make room for Fanta.

Article Title: Gurgaon homebuyer withdraws from Mahira Homes 104 project in 2023, builder promises refund but doesn't pay, consumer commission orders Rs 1.35 lakh with 9% interest and Rs 52,000 compensation
Article Text:
Czar Buildwell Pvt Ltd acknowledged that a homebuyer had not received an allotment letter or builder-buyer agreement (AI-generated image used for representative image)





GURGAON: A developer acknowledged that a homebuyer had neither received an allotment letter nor signed a builder-buyer agreement, and promised to process her refund after she withdrew from its affordable housing project.But the money remained unpaid, forcing her to approach the consumer commission, which has now ordered the builder to return Rs 1.35 lakh with interest and pay RS 52,000 in compensation and litigation costs.The district consumer disputes redressal commission, Gurgaon, held Czar Buildwell Pvt Ltd guilty of “severe deficiency in service” for failing to refund the money deposited by Vrinda Thareja, who had applied for a flat in its Mahira Homes 104 project in Sector 104 along Dwarka Expressway.Thareja applied for a unit under Haryana's Affordable Housing Policy in February 2023 and deposited Rs 1,35,298.Her name was subsequently selected in the draw, following which the developer communicated the allotment of unit T7-1704 in Tower T7 through a welcome letter dated April 25, 2023.Advocate Vaibhav Kaushik represented the complainant, said the builder then issued a demand dated April 26, 2023, asking her to deposit Rs 7,05,530 within 15 days.However, she withdrew from the project on May 15, 2023, seeking a refund of the amount already deposited.The commission noted that the developer's own Cancelled Document Receipt dated May 15, 2023, recorded that no allotment letter had been issued and no builder-buyer agreement had been executed. The document also indicated that her refund would be processed shortly.Despite this, the amount was not returned. Thareja alleged that repeated requests, followed by a legal notice sent on January 7, 2025, failed to elicit a refund.The developer did not appear before the commission despite being served and was proceeded against ex-parte.The commission president Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur said the documents placed on record corroborated the complainant's version and there was nothing to disbelieve her evidence, which remained unrebutted in the absence of the developer's defence.Allowing the complaint, the commission directed the builder to refund Rs 1,35,298 with 9% annual interest from the date of deposit until realisation. It also awarded Rs 30,000 for mental harassment, pain and agony, and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.The developer was directed to pay the awarded amount within 45 days of the order. Failure to comply would attract 12% annual interest for the stipulated period until payment.The commission also said the buyer could initiate execution proceedings and the developer could face prosecution under Section 72 of the Consumer Protection Act for non-compliance.
Article Summary: Czar Buildwell Pvt Ltd acknowledged that a homebuyer had not received an allotment letter or builder-buyer agreement. It promised to process her refund after she withdrew from its affordable housing project. But the money remained unpaid, forcing her to approach the consumer commission.

Article Title: Bengaluru man deposits Rs 2.5L in FD with cooperative society, but society stops paying after June 2024, consumer commission orders it to return Rs 2.5L with 13% interest and Rs 25k as compensation
Article Text:
(AI image) A Bengaluru commission ordered Aishwarya Co-operative Society to repay a fixed deposit of Rs 2.5 lakh.

The direction

The case

Why the commission ruled for the depositor





BENGALURU: The Bengaluru Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Aishwarya Co-operative Society Ltd to repay a 65-year-old man's Rs 2.5 lakh fixed deposit with interest at 13% per annum, holding that its failure to pay interest after June 2024 amounted to deficiency in service.In an order dated September 30, 2026, the commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, partly allowed the complaint filed by Gangadharaiah of Narasimhaiahnapalya, Magadi Main Road, against the society's president. The society, based in Rajajinagar, did not appear and was placed ex parte.The society must pay the matured FD amount of Rs 2,50,000 along with 13% annual interest from June 2024 till realisation. It must also pay Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. All dues must be cleared within 45 days of the order.The commission allowed the complaint only in part. Gangadharaiah had sought 18% interest from the date of complaint and Rs 2 lakh in damages for mental agony.Gangadharaiah said he deposited Rs 2.5 lakh with the society on July 6, 2021 at 13% interest, with the society agreeing to pay interest monthly, which came to Rs 2,700.An FD receipt (No. 062) was issued for July 6, 2021 to July 6, 2022, and the deposit was renewed (No. 988) for July 6, 2022 to July 6, 2023.The society paid interest till June 2024, he said, after which it stopped paying and did not renew the FD. His requests for renewal and the dues drew no satisfactory reply, he alleged.He wrote to the Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Societies and other authorities on November 12, 2024 and February 13, 2025, seeking payment of the principal and interest within 15 days, but got no response. A legal notice was served on July 9, 2025, which the society also did not comply with. The complaint was filed on September 24, 2025.The society did not appear despite service of notice, and filed neither a written version nor evidence. The commission relied on the complainant's affidavit and documents, including the FD certificates, letters to the registrar, the legal notice, and postal and tracking receipts.It noted that the society had accepted the deposit and agreed to pay 13% interest, and had paid it till June 2024. It said the society had not explained why it stopped paying thereafter, and that the default was a clear violation of FD terms by a financial institution.The complaint was filed under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Gangadharaiah was represented by advocate S B Vishwanath.
Article Summary: Bengaluru commission ordered Aishwarya Co-operative Society to repay a fixed deposit of Rs 2.5 lakh. The society must pay the matured FD amount of Rs2,50,000 along with 13% annual interest from June 2024 till realisation. It must also pay Rs 20,000 as compensation and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.

Article Title: IAS dreams, land cases and money lost in cyber fraud: Inside the handwritten prayer slips found in donation boxes of Agar-Malwa's Maa Baglamukhi temple, where 23 boxes hold both cash and countless wis
Article Text:
Prayer slips collected from the donation boxes are placed at the feet of Maa Baglamukhi by the priests.





UJJAIN: The donation boxes at Maa Baglamukhi temple in Nalkheda, Agar-Malwa district don’t get only cash. Devotees put in their prayers and requests too, written on paper by hand. As the counting of the boxes began on Nov 19, prayers too started tumbling out.‘Maa, make me deputy chairman,’ reads a slip. Another asks: ‘Maa, get my child engaged, make his mind settle on studies and let him become a collector.’ The list goes on.Some devotees pray for destruction of their enemies, others for an end to domestic strife, and some for a marriage to be arranged. ‘Maa, let the land case be settled and let me get it without a fight.’ ‘Maa, let the flat dispute be resolved and let the money lost in cyber crime come back.’ Susner Naib Tehsildar Rajesh Shrimal, who is overseeing the exercise, said the boxes were last opened during Chaitra Navratri.The temple management committee has installed 23 donation boxes, big and small, on the premises, and the boxes due for counting each day are brought in and emptied. Rs 20 lakh was counted from four boxes on the first day, and Rs 19 lakh from two boxes on the second.To ensure transparency, the entire process, including the bringing in of the boxes, is being videographed. About 25 bank and revenue department employees are involved. Bank staff bring a counting machine and take the day’s tally with them when office hours end.The temple management committee is given a receipt for the amount deposited. Shrimal said the currency goes with the bank staff, while the prayer slips are handed to the temple priests. The priests offer them at the feet of Maa Baglamukhi.
Article Summary: Devotees put in their prayers and requests too, written on paper by hand. The priests offer them at the feet of Maa Baglamukhi. The temple management committee has installed 23 donation boxes, big and small, on the premises, and the boxes due for counting each day.

Article Title: Bhopal car owner loses consumer case as commission upholds Rs 1 lakh insurance payout against Rs 8.22 lakh repair estimate
Article Text:
Ajeet Singh Tomar's car was severely damaged after being swept away and submerged by rainwater (AI image)





BHOPAL: A car swept away by a strong current of rainwater, partially submerged and rendered unusable ended up triggering a consumer dispute over an Rs 8.22 lakh repair estimate and an insurance settlement of just Rs 1 lakh.The car owner, who alleged that the insurer had arbitrarily rejected a major part of his claim and the authorised workshop had charged him separately for repairs, has lost his case before the Gwalior District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.Dismissing the complaint, the commission held that the owner had failed to produce technical or expert evidence establishing that all the defects in his vehicle were caused by the flooding. It also found no sufficient reason to reject the assessment of the insurance company's independent surveyor.The case involved Ajeet Singh Tomar, 44, who had insured his car, registration number MP-07-CJ-2266, with Universal Sompo General Insurance Company. The complaint was also filed against Prem Motors Pvt Ltd's Nexa service centre in Gwalior.According to the complaint, the incident occurred during the insurance period when the car was parked outside his residence.Following sudden rainfall and waterlogging, the vehicle was caught in a strong current and swept away. It was partially submerged, allowing water and mud to enter several parts of the vehicle and leaving it in a non-functional condition.The car was subsequently towed to Prem Motors' service centre, where the workshop estimated the repair cost at Rs 8,22,438.However, the insurance company, after arranging an inspection by an independent surveyor, approved only Rs 1,00,291 towards the damage. The insurer maintained that several components claimed to have been damaged were either not affected by waterlogging or were not covered under the policy.In a communication dated December 15, 2025, the insurer specifically disputed damage to components such as the clutch plate, speakers and headlight.Tomar alleged that the insurer had failed to honour the claim despite the vehicle suffering extensive damage in the incident. He further claimed that the workshop collected Rs 20,676 from him for replacing the clutch plate and other components, even though he believed the repairs should have been covered by the insurance claim.The dispute did not end with the repairs. On September 22, 2025, while returning from Mathura, Tomar reportedly encountered a battery-related problem with the car. He approached a local mechanic, who charged him Rs 1,475. The mechanic allegedly told him that nuts and bolts connected to the lithium battery had been left loose during the earlier repair work.Tomar accused the workshop of incomplete repairs and alleged that both the insurer and the service centre had indulged in deficiency of service and unfair trade practices. He sought complete repairs, a refund of Rs 20,676 and compensation for mental agony.Universal Sompo maintained that the claim had been assessed by an independent licensed surveyor and settled according to the admissible damage. It argued that the defects excluded from the claim did not match the circumstances of the reported incident and were outside the policy's coverage.Prem Motors, meanwhile, maintained that it had carried out repairs approved by the insurance company and undertaken the remaining work with the owner's consent. The commission examined the documentary evidence and affidavits before concluding that the owner's allegations were not supported by sufficient technical evidence. It observed that he had failed to establish that all the defects for which he sought reimbursement had resulted solely from the vehicle being partially submerged in floodwater.It also found no adequate grounds to disbelieve the independent surveyor's assessment, on the basis of which the insurer had approved the claim of Rs 1,00,291.On the additional Rs 20,676 collected by the workshop, the commission noted that there was no evidence establishing that the clutch plate and other components were part of the damage assessed by the surveyor. It held that charging separately for repairs beyond the approved estimate could not, by itself, establish deficiency in service.The commission, headed by president Rajendra Prasad Sharma, dismissed the complaint on November 13, 2026, and directed both sides to bear their own litigation expenses.
Article Summary: Ajeet Singh Tomar, 44, had insured his car, registration number MP-07-CJ-2266, with Universal Sompo General Insurance Company. He alleged that the insurer had arbitrarily rejected a major part of his claim and the authorised workshop had charged him separately for repairs.

Article Title: Booking a flight on the day of departure costs Rs 858 more than a day earlier at median, same-day fare higher on 64.8% of route-days across 54 routes, Pune to Chennai sees 32.6% jump
Article Text:
Flight fares in India increase sharply within the last 24 hours before departure, impacting travelers' choices and budgets (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)

The last 24 hours before a flight are the most expensive hours in Indian aviation. On one route the same-day fare runs a third above the day-before price.

The last day is its own price bracket

Median fare across 54 routes: bought the day before, against bought on the day

And it is not occasional

Where the last day costs most

Last-minute flight bookings carry a premium, with same-day fares on Pune-Chennai routes costing 32.6% more than earlier bookings

Every route, ranked by the cost of deciding one day later

What it means for you

The Short Version

About This Data





Most advice about booking flights talks in weeks and months. The sharpest jump in the whole booking curve happens inside a single day.Across 211 days and 54 routes, the median same-day fare is Rs 9,041. The fare for the same route bought one day earlier is Rs 8,183.That is Rs 858, or seven per cent at the median route-day, for a decision made 24 hours later.The same-day fare is higher than the day-before fare on 64.8% of route-days we measured. So roughly two times in three, waiting one more night costs you money.The remaining third is where it gets interesting. Sometimes a seat that has not sold is dumped on the morning of departure, and the walk-up fare drops below yesterday's. That is the gamble, and it loses twice as often as it wins.Pune to Chennai carries the steepest same-day penalty in the country at 32.6%. Pune to Ahmedabad is 24.3%, Ahmedabad to Hyderabad 21.2, Delhi to Ahmedabad 19.8.These are thin routes with few daily departures. When there are five flights rather than fifteen, the last unsold seats carry more of the aircraft's cost, and the pricing reflects it.If you are weighing up a trip and the departure is tomorrow, the decision is worth making tonight rather than in the morning. On an average route that is Rs 858.If your route is a thin one, particularly anything involving Pune or Ahmedabad on a secondary pairing, it is worth considerably more than that.And if you are holding out for a last-minute drop, understand the odds. It happens about a third of the time.The median same-day fare in India is Rs 9,041. The same seat bought the previous day is Rs 8,183.That is Rs 858, or 7%, for waiting one more night. It happens on 64.8% of route-days.Pune to Chennai is the worst, at 32.6%. Thin routes with few daily flights carry the steepest penalty.A last-minute drop does happen, but only about a third of the time.Same-day fares are recorded on the morning of departure and compared with the fare recorded for that same flight date 24 hours earlier.The Airline Fare Tracker records the median fare shown on Google Flights for 54 routes between Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune.Fares are captured every day, and this analysis covers 211 consecutive days from 28 April to 24 November 2026 with no missing dates. The index sets every route to 100 on 28 April and weights routes by monthly scheduled seats.Limits. These are advertised medians, not fares finally paid. All eight cities are metros, so smaller routes are not measured.There is no year-earlier comparison yet, so changes across the period cannot be separated from seasonal demand or from the fuel-driven capacity reduction that sits inside it.Roughly 6% of daily readings were filled in by the data provider where a capture failed. The tracker records which airline flies a route but not which airline charged a given fare.
Article Summary: The last 24 hours before a flight are the most expensive hours in Indian aviation. On one route the same-day fare runs a third above the day-before price. Pune to Chennai is the worst, at 32.6%. Thin routes with few daily flights carry the steepest penalty.

Article Title: Pune techie lists used mattress online for Rs 15,000, receives QR code from prospective buyer to collect payment, scans it repeatedly after being told transactions failed and loses Rs 3.97 lakh
Article Text:
(AI image) An IT professional from Phursungi lost Rs 3.97 lakh while attempting to sell a used mattress online





PUNE: An attempt to sell a used mattress online ended up costing an IT professional nearly Rs 4 lakh. The 46-year-old from Phursungi listed the mattress on an online marketplace and was taken in by a fraudster posing as a prospective buyer. He was tricked into scanning QR codes to receive the payment, but each scan resulted in money being debited from his bank account.The fraud took place in Aug and the man lodged a complaint with the Phursungi police on Monday.An officer said on Aug 10, the complainant listed his mattress for Rs 15,000. A man contacted him through the platform and expressed interest in buying it.“The ‘buyer’ took the complainant’s mobile number, said he would make the payment next day and send someone to collect the mattress,” the officer said.According to the complaint, on Aug 11, the suspect sent the complainant a QR code, claiming it was linked to his merchant account and that all he needed to do to receive the payment was to scan it. “He was told that the transaction might initially fail,” the officer said.The man scanned the code using a UPI app and received Rs 2, leading him to believe the process was genuine. “However, when he scanned another code, Rs 15,000 was debited from his account,” the officer said.The fraudster then claimed the payment had failed and persuaded the techie to repeat the process. Believing the earlier transactions would be reversed, he continued scanning QR codes, and losing money.“Seven transactions were carried out on Aug 11, resulting in a total loss of Rs 3.97 lakh. The fraudster subsequently stopped responding to calls and blocked the victim’s number,” the officer said.“We have sought the details of the transactions from his bank,” the officer said.
Article Summary: An IT professional from Phursungi lost Rs 3.97 lakh while attempting to sell a used mattress online. The 46-year-old listed the mattress on an online marketplace and was taken in by a fraudster posing as a prospective buyer. He was tricked into scanning QR codes to receive the payment, but each scan resulted in money being debited.

Article Title: Bengaluru woman’s Rs 12.7 lakh Groww portfolio falls to Rs 84,508 after tech glitch during Rs 10 lakh withdrawal; firm told to refund Rs 11.85 lakh with 6% interest and pay Rs 12,000
Article Text:
(Representative) Ranjana Priya's investment of Rs 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished, reaching Rs 12.7 lakhs





BENGALURU: Imagine watching your savings grow to over Rs 12 lakh on an investment app, only to see the balance shrink to under Rs 1 lakh the moment you try to withdraw your own money. That is what a city woman faced when the Groww app displayed a sudden, unexplained error after she sought a redemption. The Bengaluru (Urban) District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held the platform liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The saga began when Ranjana Priya, a resident of HSR Layout, Sector 2, trusted the platform's market reputation and assurances and invested a total of Rs 8.12 lakhs through systematic investment plans (SIPs) on the Groww app. Favourable market performance pushed her portfolio up significantly, and the official dashboard showed its valuation had reached Rs 12,70,404 as of November 26, 2025.Citing urgent personal and financial requirements, she placed a digital request for a partial redemption of Rs 10 lakh. What followed, she said, were "alarming errors". The dashboard updated to show her total invested amount as just Rs 84,508, wiping out the rest of her portfolio value.Priya said she ran from pillar to post, raising support tickets by phone and email and complaining to SEBI on November 27. Nothing was resolved.On November 30, Groww credited a mere Rs 15,500 to her bank account. By her reconciliation, her total investment value stood at Rs 12.70 lakhs. After accounting for the amount redeemed, Rs 11.85 lakhs was left unaccounted for.She then raised statutory grievances on the e-Jagriti platform through WhatsApp four times between December 7 and December 25, 2025. The opposite parties neither corrected their financial records nor refunded the balance. Leaving her with no option, Priya approached the commission on April 22, 2026, and sought a refund for mental agony, harassment and financial hardship.She named Groww Invest Tech Pvt Ltd and Nextbillion Technology Pvt Ltd (Groww)/Billionbrains Garage Ventures Pvt Ltd. Both appeared through counsel but did not file their written version within the statutory 45 days. Their version was taken as not filed, in line with a judgment of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, and despite sufficient opportunities, they never mounted a defence.After going through the records and hearing arguments, the commission observed that her allegations stood unchallenged as the firms had forfeited their right to defence. It accepted as true her digital records, including the portfolio value of Rs 12.7 lakhs and the redemption request for Rs 10 lakh. The platform's act of reducing the visible portfolio value to Rs 84,508, coupled with its complete failure to respond to four separate institutional warnings from the National Grievance Helpline, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, it said. It termed the withholding of Rs 11.85 lakhs belonging to a retail investor "completely unauthorised, illegal and high handed".The commission added that a digital investment platform cannot hold a consumer's hard-earned savings hostage under the guise of an unrectified technical glitch or internal database error. The documents showed beyond doubt that of her Rs 12. 7 lakhs portfolio, Rs 11.85 lakhs remained unaccounted for and was withheld without valid legal justification, causing mental agony and financial distress to a complainant dependent on her savings.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra MS and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani directed both firms, jointly and severally, to refund Rs 11,85,896 with 6% annual interest from the date of redemption until actual realisation. It further ordered them to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service and mental harassment and Rs 2,000 as litigation costs.
Article Summary: Ranjana Priya's investment of Rs 8.12 lakhs in the Groww app initially flourished. She placed a digital request for a partial redemption of Rs 10 lakh. What followed, she said, were "alarming errors" The dashboard updated to show her total invested amount as just Rs 84,508.

Article Title: Bengaluru man relocates from Chennai, pays Voltas Rs 1,770 to reinstall AC, technicians damage it during reinstallation, consumer commission orders Voltas to pay Rs 33,770 compensation
Article Text:
A Bengaluru consumer commission ruled that Voltas Ltd must compensate a customer for air conditioner damage.





BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer after finding deficiency in service by its technicians, who allegedly damaged his air conditioner while reinstalling it after he relocated from Chennai.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban) directed the company to pay Rs 25,000 as consolidated compensation for the damage and operational loss of the AC, along with 3% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint.It also ordered a refund of Rs 1,770 towards installation charges, Rs 5,000 for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 2,000 towards litigation expenses.The commission directed Voltas to comply with the order within 45 days.According to the complaint filed by S Balaji, 37, his Voltas 1.5-tonne split AC (Model 183SY) was in working condition when it was dismantled in Chennai in March 2025. A technical fitness report issued by Dynamic Cool Center had certified that the unit was functional before it was moved to Bengaluru.After relocating, Balaji approached Voltas for reinstallation on April 19, 2025, and paid Rs 1,770 for the service. He alleged that the technicians deployed by the company lacked the necessary expertise and leaked the entire refrigerant gas charge during the installation process, leaving the machine non-functional.The complaint stated that Voltas technicians returned on May 1 and refilled the refrigerant gas without charging him. However, Balaji alleged that they left the cooling system unpressurised and exposed, allowing atmospheric moisture to enter over the next 12 days. This allegedly damaged the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and fan motor.Despite raising multiple service requests and escalating the matter through emails, the AC developed recurring reset problems and eventually stopped functioning completely. Balaji also approached the National Consumer Helpline, but his grievances were marked as disposed of without a technical resolution.The commission noted that the complainant had submitted documents establishing that the AC was functional before its relocation and that it developed major defects following the reinstallation carried out by Voltas. It also observed that the company had failed to provide any contrary technical evidence or written explanation." The deployment of untrained staff and the subsequent terminal damage to the machine amounts to a deficiency of service," the commission observed.However, it declined to award the full original purchase value of Rs 33,000 sought by Balaji, noting that the AC was not brand new when it was reinstalled in Bengaluru and had already been used in Chennai. It said awarding the full purchase value without accounting for depreciation would be inequitable.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra M S and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, passed the order on September 30, 2026. Voltas and its Bengaluru branch manager did not appear before the commission despite service of notice and were proceeded against ex parte.
Article Summary: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed Voltas Ltd to pay Rs 33,770 to a customer after finding deficiency in service by its technicians. S Balaji, 37, alleged that the technicians deployed by the company lacked the necessary expertise and leaked the entire refrigerant gas charge during the installation process.

Article Title: Delhi SIR: Last day to file claims, objections on Wednesday; final roll on December 22
Article Text:
Wednesday marks the final opportunity for voters to file claims and objections regarding the electoral roll.





NEW DELHI: Wednesday will be the last day for filing claims and objections under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral roll. The final roll will be published on Dec 22.The office of the chief electoral officer (CEO) Tuesday said Delhi had received 3.3 lakh applications seeking inclusion of names in the voter list since Aug 31 when the SIR draft electoral roll was published and nearly 47.6 lakh voters were left out of around 1.45 crore listed in the last roll. It contained around 97.5 lakh names. SIR began in Delhi on June 30.The CEO office said 3.3 lakh Form 6 applications were received between Aug 31 and Nov 23. Form 6 is used for inclusion of names in the electoral rolls. The office also received 35,155 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of names and 1.2 lakh Form 8 applications for corrections in voter details, shifting of residence or replacement of EPIC cards. Another 610 Form 6A applications came from overseas electors seeking registration."No further extension of the claims and objections period was likely as the electoral roll revision process has to be completed within the revised schedule," said an official.The original deadline of Oct 30 was extended last month till Nov 25 to allow additional time to the deleted as well as first-time voters.Among districts, West recorded the highest number of Form 6 applications at 39,792, followed by North East (32,341), North West (31,375), East (31,359) and South East (31,518). New Delhi recorded the lowest number at 5,741.South East district received the highest number of Form 7 applications at 4,808, followed by South (4,719), North East (4,305) and West (3,614). For Form 8, North East topped the list with 16,729 applications, followed by West (12,999), East (12,718) and South West (11,927).The deadline extension pushed back the subsequent stages of the revision. The deadline for disposal of claims and objections was pushed from Nov 30 to Dec 15, while publication of the final electoral roll was rescheduled from Dec 4 to 22.
Article Summary: Wednesday will be the last day for filing claims and objections under the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral roll. The final roll will be published on Dec 22. Nearly 47.6 lakh voters were left out of around 1.45 crore listed in the last roll.

Article Title: Live close, score more: Delhi schools give up to 90 points for neighbourhood
Article Text:
Delhi private schools are changing nursery admission criteria for the upcoming 2027-28 academic session (AI image)

Many schools assign significant points based on neighbourhood proximity to applicants.





NEW DELHI: Where a child lives is emerging as one of the biggest factors in nursery admission criteria set by several Delhi private schools for the 2027-28 academic session.Some schools have set aside 50 to 70 of the 100 available points for neighbourhood proximity, while the weightage goes up to 90 at a few schools. Having a sibling already enrolled or a parent who studied at the school can also fetch additional points.DPS Vasant Vihar and DPS East of Kailash award up to 50 points for neighbourhood proximity. Having a sibling at either campus or at DPS RK Puram earns an applicant 26 points, while each eligible parent who is a DPS RK Puram alumnus gets 12 points.“Neighbourhood proximity carries up to 50 points, measured by aerial distance from the respective campus. Applicants living within 6 km get 50 points, with the score falling to 20 beyond 15 km,” said a member of the DPS school administration.Vasant Valley School’s admission criteria also give weight to neighbourhood proximity, along with sibling and alumni categories. Tagore International School, too, considers the distance between a child’s residence and the school, whether a sibling is enrolled and whether a parent studied there.Applications for open seats in nursery, lower KG, upper KG and Class I, wherever schools offer fresh admissions, will open on Dec 1 and close on Dec 28.Directorate of Education (DoE) has directed private unaided recognised schools to upload their admission criteria and points allotted to each by Nov 26. The first selection list is due on Jan 20.Annexure 3 of the DoE circular lists more than 60 criteria that schools cannot use to award points. These include transferable jobs or inter-state transfers, parents’ educational qualifications, a parent working at a sister-concern school, both parents working and whether a child has a first cousin studying at the school.Among the more unusual prohibited criteria are “Vegetarianism”, “Non-smoker parent”, “Non-alcoholic”, “Joint Family” and “Similar cultural ethos”. Schools also cannot award points for significant non-financial contributions or volunteering by a parent or grandparent.MM Public School in Pitampura gives 60 points to applicants living within 12 km and 20 points to girl applicants. It awards 10 points each for a sibling already enrolled and a parent who studied there.Dwarka International School gives 90 points for applicants living within a road distance of 10 km and five points to first-born children.Mamta Modern School gives 70 points to applicants living within 1 km, 60 points for those in the 1-3 km band and 50 for those living 3-5 km away. Applicants living 5 km or farther away get 40 points. The school also awards 20 points for a sibling already enrolled and 10 under the alumni criterion.“We have adopted these criteria as they are standard, commonly followed, and in line with the guidelines prescribed by the Directorate of Education, ensuring fairness and uniformity in the admission process,” said Pallavi Sharma of Mamta Modern School.The DoE circular also refers to its 2016 order that originally abolished 62 admission criteria. A Delhi High Court interim order stayed its operation with respect to 11 criteria, including first-born status and gender, as well as the management quota.
Article Summary: Some schools have set aside 50 to 70 of the 100 available points for neighbourhood proximity. Having a sibling already enrolled or a parent who studied at the school can also fetch additional points. The Directorate of Education (DoE) has directed private unaided recognised schools to upload their admission criteria by Nov 26.

Wall Street retreated on Tuesday as technology stocks gave back some of the previous day's sharp gains, with investors booking profits and turning cautious ahead of key US inflation data. Nvidia and Anthropic led the decline in AI-linked stocks.The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. However, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 423.39 points, or 0.85%, to 50,018.70.The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound, however, failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.Anthropic shares tumbled 6.5% to $81.90, slipping below their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83, just days after the AI startup's record-breaking Nasdaq debut.The stock opened at $111.50 on November 19, with its fully diluted valuation briefly exceeding $2 trillion. However, it has since lost ground amid a broader technology selloff.Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its IPO after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares, making it the biggest public offering on record and surpassing SpaceX's $85.7 billion listing in June.CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth over $280 million a day after the IPO, according to a filing late on Monday.The company's rapid reversal has renewed concerns about elevated AI valuations and the massive investments being made in computing infrastructure, particularly as higher interest rates could increase financing costs, Reuters reported.Anthropic is not the first major technology company to fall below its IPO price soon after listing. SpaceX took about a month to slip below its offer price, while Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its IPO price on its second trading day in 2012.Nvidia shares fell 5.9% as investors reassessed the implications of Jensen Huang's return as CEO and the political and governance risks surrounding the company.The chipmaker had surged nearly 30% on Monday after Huang's reinstatement, helping the S&P 500 and Nasdaq post their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025.Technology stocks led the declines on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 technology sector falling 2.8%. The semiconductor index dropped 7.9%, reflecting renewed selling in AI-linked companies.Before Monday's rally, AI stocks had struggled for weeks as investors questioned whether the sector's debt-fuelled spending on infrastructure would generate sufficient returns.Investors are also looking ahead to Wednesday's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge watched by the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting.Persistent inflation has strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. Fed funds futures traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a rate hike in December and a 66% chance of another increase in January, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said late on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point towards tighter monetary policy.Investors were also wary of potential new tariffs after Reuters reported, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a probe into alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 major US trading partners. The findings are expected to pave the way for new import duties on a wide range of goods.The administration's tariffs have contributed to higher consumer prices in the US, adding to inflation concerns.The dollar fell 0.44% against a basket of major currencies, retreating from a 20-month high touched earlier in the session.The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes edged up 0.77 basis points to 4.928%, compared with 4.92% late on Monday.The gap between two-year and 10-year Treasury yields, a closely watched indicator of economic expectations, stood at 24.3 basis points.Gold futures fell 2.67% and silver futures dropped 5.75%, pressured by hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials and expectations of higher interest rates.Brent crude futures settled $2.03 higher, or 2.27%, at $91.40 a barrel after a volatile session, with fresh attacks reported on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the S&P 500 declined 0.50% to 7,201.09. The pullback came a day after Wall Street staged a strong rally, driven by Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO. The rebound failed to ease concerns over stretched AI valuations, rising infrastructure spending and the outlook for interest rates.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500 million, following the latter's blockbuster debut on the Nasdaq, according to a report by Focus Taiwan.TSMC's subsidiary, TSMC Partners, purchased 6,024,096 shares in Anthropic at $83 apiece, the same price at which the AI company offered its shares in its initial public offering ( IPO ). TSMC disclosed the transaction in a filing on Thursday.The purchase was primarily an equity investment, with the payment to be made in a lump sum under Rule 144 of the US Securities Act of 1933, the report said.The investment follows a November 10 decision by TSMC's board to approve investments of up to $500 million each in Anthropic's common shares and preferred shares of OpenAI Group, the company behind ChatGPT.While the latest transaction confirms TSMC's investment in Anthropic, the separate authorisation for OpenAI highlights the chipmaker's interest in two major companies developing artificial intelligence systems.Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI assistant, made its Nasdaq debut on November 19 after raising approximately $81.34 billion through its IPO. The offering comprised 980 million shares priced at $83 apiece, making it the largest IPO on record and one of the biggest public listings in the technology sector.The company's shares opened at $111.50, a premium of 34.34% over the IPO price, and climbed to an intraday high of $115.10 before paring gains. They eventually closed at $97.17, up 17.07% from the offering price.At the closing price, Anthropic's fully diluted market valuation stood at $1.76 trillion, after briefly crossing $2 trillion during the opening minutes of trading. Following its much-anticipated market debut, the company's market capitalisation was also reported at approximately $1.44 trillion, against an IPO valuation of around $1.5 trillion.Based in San Francisco, Anthropic trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.TSMC's investment comes at a time when artificial intelligence companies are attracting significant investor capital. Anthropic's strong market debut reflected this interest, with its shares closing well above their IPO price.However, the growing investments in the sector have also come amid concerns over a possible AI bubble, high valuations, rising infrastructure costs and the sustainability of AI-related investments.
Article Summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has acquired a 0.03% stake in US-based artificial intelligence company Anthropic for approximately $500 million. Article Title: Gurgaon couple buys sandals for Rs 2,429, heel bends on first use, showroom refuses replacement and offers repairs, consumer commission orders full refund with 9% interest and Rs 26,000 compensation a
Article Text:
(AI IMAGE) Deepak Gupta and his wife Shweta faced a not-so-great experience with defective sandals right after they bought them





GURGAON: A pair of sandals bought for Rs 2,429 developed a defect on its first use, but when the buyers approached the showroom, they were offered repairs instead of a replacement. Rejecting the footwear company’s repair-only warranty policy, the Gurgaon consumer commission has ordered it to refund the purchase price and pay Rs 26,000 in compensation and litigation costs.Deepak Gupta and his wife Shweta bought the sandals from Stelatoes Shoes & Accessories Pvt Ltd’s Gurudwara Road showroom on Aug 30, 2025. The salesperson allegedly assured them that the footwear was a fresh piece and carried a six-month replacement warranty in case of any defect.However, when Shweta wore the sandals for the first time on Sept 1, the heel bent and the adhesive came loose, the couple alleged. They returned to the showroom on Sept 3, but the manager allegedly blamed the damage on her twisting her foot and refused to replace the footwear, offering only repairs.After their repeated requests for a refund went unanswered, the couple approached the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.Advocate Chandan Yadav, representing the complainants, relied on their affidavit, purchase invoice and photographs of the sandals. The company’s authorised representative, Akshay Sharma, argued that the terms printed on the invoice excluded refunds and allowed only repairs within the 90-day warranty period. He said the company was willing to repair the footwear.The commission, headed by president Sanjeev Jindal with members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur, rejected the defence, observing that a company could not benefit from its own wrongdoing after selling poor-quality goods. It held that unilateral warranty conditions placing consumers at a disadvantage could not override their rights.The panel also noted that the company failed to produce any evidence to rebut the complainants’ allegations. Holding that the company had committed deficiency in service and adopted an unfair trade practice, it allowed the complaint.The opposite parties were directed to refund Rs 2,428.99 with 9% annual interest from Aug 30, 2025, and pay Rs 15,000 for mental harassment and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.
Article Summary: Deepak Gupta and his wife Shweta bought the sandals from Stelatoes Shoes & Accessories Pvt Ltd’s Gurudwara Road showroom on Aug 30, 2025. The salesperson allegedly assured them that the footwear was a fresh piece and carried a six- month replacement warranty in case of any defect. The heel bent and the adhesive came loose, the couple alleged. The manager allegedly blamed the damage on her twisting her foot and offered only repairs.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: What billionaires paid nearly $400 million to stop in California has existed in Norway since 1892
Article Text:
Norway’s model: broad, low and modest

US proposals target fewer than 1,000 people at steep rates

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A constitutional hurdle Norway never faced

Earlier this month, a group of billionaires, including Google co-founder Sergey Brin, collaborated and spent $378 million to defeat Prop 40 – a one-time tax on billionaires. But Norway introduced a wealth tax back in 1892 – when the US was deep in the Gilded Age, an era when industrialists like John D. Rockefeller and Andrew Carnegie amassed unprecedented fortunes amid stark economic inequality. Now more than 130 years later, the country still collects that tax even as the US is once again grappling with extreme wealth concentration that by some measures surpasses Gilded Age levels, Fortune reported. While both countries debate taxing net worth, they are working from fundamentally different blueprints, a gap that shapes how much money a wealth tax raises, who leaves the country, and whether it can survive legal challenges.Unlike US proposals aimed squarely at billionaires, Norway’s wealth tax applies to a wide swath of the population, including middle-class homeowners and savers with substantial assets and low debt.As per 2026 tax rates, net wealth above NOK 1.9 million (roughly $197,000) is taxed at a combined local and national rate of 1%, with the threshold doubled for married couples. Above NOK 21.5 million (about $2.2 million), the rate edges up to 1.1%.According to Tax Foundation economist Cristina Enache, the levy generated roughly 0.6% of Norway’s GDP and 1.5% of total tax revenue in 2024 – a relatively small share that leads economists to caution against assuming a US version would produce massive windfalls.Although total revenue from the tax has continued to climb despite an exodus of millionaires, a poll ahead of Norway’s September 2025 election showed 39% of Norwegians favored keeping or raising it, 23% wanted it reduced, and 28% wanted it abolished. Economists also note that Norway’s massive sovereign wealth fund – the largest in the world – is built primarily on petroleum taxes, licensing fees, and state ownership interests rather than wealth-tax receipts.In contrast, leading American proposals focused narrowly on ultra-high-net-worth individuals at a much higher rate. The Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act, introduced by Sanders and Khanna in March, would levy a 5% annual tax on Americans worth more than $1 billion – a group of 938 people by the sponsors' count.Projected revenue from a 5% federal billionaire tax varies sharply depending on assumptions around tax avoidance. Sanders and Khanna cite estimates from economists Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman projecting $4.4 trillion over a decade to fund $3,000 direct payments to households earning $150,000 or less, alongside housing, health care, and childcare programs.Assuming higher rates of avoidance and factoring in compliance costs, the Tax Foundation estimates a 5% tax above $1 billion would bring in roughly $1.5 trillion over 10 years, or about $3.3 trillion under alternative assumptions applied to the Sanders-Khanna bill.Beyond enforcement and valuation headaches, a federal wealth tax in the US faces a constitutional barrier that does not exist in Norway. While states are permitted to tax wealth, the US Constitution requires “direct” federal taxes to be apportioned among the states by population, with the 16th Amendment carving out an exception only for taxes on income.Legal watchers closely followed the 2024 Supreme Court ruling in Moore v. United States, which involved a dispute over unrealized income. Although the court ruled on narrow grounds without deciding the constitutionality of a wealth tax, four justices – just one short of a majority – signaled that income must be realised before it can be taxed.
Article Summary: US proposals target fewer than 1,000 people at steep rates. Norway's wealth tax applies to a wide swath of the population, including middle-class homeowners and savers with substantial assets and low debt. A federal wealth tax in the US faces a constitutional barrier that does not exist in Norway.

Article Title: Report claims Elon Musk made $500,000 donation to Austin to help homeless young adults find homes; Tesla CEO responds

Austin secures matching funds from Musk Foundation

Programme focused on former foster youth

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has confirmed reports that the Musk Foundation contributed $500,000 to a City of Austin initiative which is aimed at helping homeless young adults who have aged out of the foster care system secure housing and support services. This development came after a widely shared post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) highlighted the contribution, claiming that Musk had donated $500,000 to help homeless young adults so that they can find homes in Austin. The funding is said to help as many as 100 young adults access housing assistance and supportive services as they transition from foster care to independent living.The city officials also claimed that the young adults leaving foster care often face some really hard challenges when it comes to securing housing because they may lack the financial resources and family support networks available to many of their peers.The new funding by the Musk Foundation is intended to address those barriers and offer pathways to long-term stability.Earlier this year, City Council Member Ryan Alter, who represents District 5, secured $500,000 in the city’s 2026-27 budget for housing help for former foster youth. The money was contingent on the city finding $500,000 in matching funds. With the Musk Foundation’s contribution, the full $1 million can now proceed.“Every young person deserves a strong foundation,” said David Gray, director of Austin Homeless Strategies and Operations, saying the investment gives 100 young adults a meaningful housing opportunity. Mayor Kirk Watson said the investment supports his Generation ATX initiative, which aims to expand opportunities for the city’s next generation. Alter said the funds will help young people sleep out of extreme heat, cold or rain, and will save taxpayers from supporting them for decades.The donation attracted attention on social media after an X user highlighted the city announcement and praised the contribution. Musk later responded to the post, stating, “This news is accurate,” confirming that the reported donation had indeed been made.The contribution comes as Austin continues to expand housing assistance programmes for former foster youth, with officials saying the combined public-private investment will help more young adults secure stable housing and access wraparound support services.
