Article Title: Political tensions, AI-powered attacks to dominate APAC cyber threat landscape in 2027: Kaspersky
Article Text:
Geopolitical tensions to fuel cyber espionage

AI-powered cyberattacks expected to become more sophisticated

India's elections and local supply chains in focus

Post-quantum transition may attract nation-state actors

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Regulatory changes may create new targets

Security measures recommended

Geopolitical rivalries, regional conflicts and the growing use of artificial intelligence by cybercriminals are expected to play a major role in shaping the Asia-Pacific (APAC) cybersecurity landscape in 2027, according to Kaspersky’s Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT). The cybersecurity company said that while rapid advances in AI will continue to influence cyberattacks, persistent political and regional tensions across APAC are likely to remain the most significant drivers of advanced persistent threat (APT) activity next year. The region has increasingly become a target for state-linked cyber groups seeking diplomatic, strategic and financial gains, with sectors such as aviation, finance and government infrastructure frequently in the crosshairs.Sergey Lozhkin, Head of Kaspersky's Research Center for the Asia-Pacific and Middle East, Türkiye and Africa regions, said APAC's position as both a hub of digital transformation and a region marked by geopolitical tensions makes it a prime target for sophisticated cyber operations.According to Kaspersky, organisations across both the public and private sectors should prepare for continued cyber espionage campaigns targeting defence, telecommunications and critical infrastructure.The company also warned that territorial disputes and political instability in parts of the region could lead to an increase in hacktivist campaigns and targeted phishing attacks aimed at influencing public opinion and local narratives.Kaspersky researchers expect AI weaponisation to mature significantly in 2027, enabling attackers to automate larger portions of the cyber kill chain. Threat actors are likely to deploy AI-powered systems capable of conducting reconnaissance, identifying vulnerabilities and launching intrusions with minimal human intervention.The company said the time between vulnerability disclosure and exploitation could shrink to just a few days, providing attackers with a faster path to compromise systems. Small and medium-sized businesses are expected to become increasingly attractive targets due to limited cybersecurity resources, while larger enterprises may face more stealthy and difficult-to-detect attacks.Kaspersky also predicts that advanced threat groups will increasingly leverage open-source large language models to generate spear-phishing campaigns, create exploit code and conduct deepfake-enabled social engineering attacks targeting senior executives and government officials.For India, Kaspersky believes several domestic developments could significantly influence cyber threats in 2027. Among them are upcoming state elections in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa, Manipur, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, along with the Presidential election scheduled for July.Saurabh Sharma, Lead Security Researcher at Kaspersky GReAT, said these political events could become focal points for cyber operations involving deepfakes, phishing campaigns and influence operations targeting political parties and campaign staff.The company also highlighted risks emerging from India's expanding "Make in India" manufacturing ecosystem. As more domestic suppliers, vendors and manufacturers become integrated into strategic industries such as defence, electronics and telecommunications, attackers may increasingly target supply chains to gain access to critical systems.According to Sharma, threat actors are expected to focus on compromising open-source software components, firmware updates and trusted software-as-a-service platforms used by Indian organisations, particularly those operated by smaller Tier-2 and Tier-3 vendors with weaker cybersecurity controls.Kaspersky further warned that India's early adoption of post-quantum cryptography could draw the attention of nation-state-backed threat groups.As critical infrastructure organisations begin piloting post-quantum algorithms, attackers may intensify "harvest now, decrypt later" operations, in which encrypted information is stolen today with the expectation that future quantum computing capabilities could eventually unlock the data.The company said current encryption standards such as RSA and ECC remain widely used across digital communications, but advances in quantum computing have prompted governments and enterprises worldwide to prepare for cryptographic migration.The report also noted that increasing regulatory requirements and data localisation mandates could reshape India's cyber risk environment. Regulations such as the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) are prompting organisations to store more sensitive information locally, creating larger repositories of valuable data that may attract nation-state adversaries.Sharma said businesses should not assume regulatory compliance alone will protect them from sophisticated attacks. Instead, organisations need to focus on identifying where critical data resides, implementing strong encryption and access controls, and monitoring network traffic for potential data exfiltration attempts.To mitigate evolving cyber threats, Kaspersky urged organisations to maintain robust patch management practices, deploy advanced threat detection and incident response technologies, and invest in regular cybersecurity awareness training.The company noted that spear-phishing remains one of the most common entry points for APT campaigns, making employee education a critical layer of defence against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.
Article Summary: Geopolitical rivalries, regional conflicts and the growing use of artificial intelligence are expected to play a major role in shaping the Asia-Pacific (APAC) cybersecurity landscape in 2027. Kaspersky warned that territorial disputes and political instability in parts of the region could lead to an increase in hacktivist campaigns and targeted phishing attacks. The cybersecurity company said rapid advances in AI will continue to influence cyberattacks.

Article Title: Bill Gates and Melinda French got divorced in May 2021, everything about the divorce settlement has been kept secret, except this one 'Microsoft number'
Article Text:
Melinda French and Bill Gates

What was the $1.8 billion stock transfer

Why did Bill Gates transfer shares instead of cash

Why stock worth $100,000 may not mean $100,000 in cash

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates announced their divorce in May 2021, they kept the financial details of their separation private. The former couple did not publicly reveal how their estimated fortune was divided or whether they had signed a prenuptial agreement. However, one major figure emerged from public filings: around $1.8 billion worth of stock transferred to Melinda French Gates from Cascade Investment on May 3, 2021. The investment firm was built using money Bill Gates earned through Microsoft dividends and share sales, making the transfer a notable link between the couple's divorce and the tech billionaire's Microsoft wealth.According to public filings, Cascade Investment transferred around 14.1 million shares of Canadian National Railway and nearly 3 million shares of AutoNation to Melinda French Gates. At the time, the holdings were valued at approximately $1.5 billion and $309 million, respectively.The transfers did not stop there. On May 13, 2021, Cascade also transferred around $851 million worth of Deere & Co. stock to her. Forbes' review of SEC filings found that publicly disclosed stock transfers to Melinda had crossed $3 billion by then.The timing of the transfers suggests they were connected to the divorce settlement, although the exact terms of the agreement have never been made public.There is a financial reason why couples may choose to transfer investments directly during a divorce rather than sell them and divide the money. Under US federal tax law, transfers of property between spouses, or former spouses as part of a divorce, are generally not taxable at the time of transfer.“The biggest reason is taxes,” family mediator and Certified Divorce Financial Analyst Kristyn Carmichael told Moneywise.She explained that selling shares worth $1.8 billion to pay the other spouse in cash could create a large capital gains tax bill for the seller.Carmichael also warned that people receiving shares in a divorce should check what the original owner paid for them. “$100,000 in stock is not the same as $100,000 in cash,” she said.For example, if someone receives shares worth $100,000 that their spouse originally bought for $10,000, selling them could mean paying taxes on the $90,000 gain.Michelle Smith, a certified divorce financial analyst, also advised couples to compare investments after accounting for taxes. “If you take lower-basis stock while your spouse keeps cash, you may have taken the smaller half without realizing it,” she told Moneywise.
Article Summary: $1.8 billion worth of stock transferred to Melinda French Gates from Cascade Investment on May 3, 2021. Cascade Investment was built using money Bill Gates earned through Microsoft dividends and share sales. On May 13, 2021, Cascade also transferred around $851 million worth of Deere & Co. stock to her.
